steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Honorable lady, I'm most privileged to inform you, the dinner party is all ready—
So slow. You aristocrats, taking your sweet time with everything you do. You're a nightmare.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: ...It was my inadequate reception. Please, permit that I express to you my most sincere apologies.
You can save your breath. How many will be coming today, exactly?

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: All of County Hillock's fine minds have received the invitation, including our most widely celebrated bard as of recent, Seamus Williams...
Bard? I'm bored dead already. What about the nobles and merchants you promised to find?

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Of course... of course, they'll all be coming too.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: For example, the leader within the south region's textiles industry, Sir Paulet, recipient of the McCaughey Prize, Dr. Bashir, and the owner of more than ten steelworks, Mr. Evans...
Oh? These people you mention, especially that last one, they're definitely coming?

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Yes, and a portion of them have already arrived.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: I hear a most honorable guest has turned up, and quite a few celebrity intellects from other cities have come flocking too, all for a single glimpse of you and your compatriots' presence.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Oh, yes, as per your request, I've drawn up this list of names, for your perusal whenever you should—
Bit too many words, but you've done good enough work. Alright, you can head off now.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Deeply grateful for your generous praise. Once you're ready, please, inform me. I simply cannot wait to see this ordinary little parlor of mine be dazzlingly belightened by your arrival.
Why are you still here? Weren't you done talking?

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Ahem, please allow me to ask one last question—that most honorable lady there, have we even the sliver of a chance that she may alight on the venue too?
That's not yours to ask. Clear off.
Mandragora, what has you feeling all flustered?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Less of that—tongue-in-cheek, giving me reflux. We all know you'd never really give a shit about anyone, Harmonie.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Siiigh. Then I'll have to put it another way—you've been blocking my light with your halfwit ambling. I'd like to finish reading this lovely novel, dear.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Tch.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Are all of you rich people like this?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Hang instruments up a wall, buy a few books, act like you're filling the windows so nobody notices how you've got nothing at all in your head.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: I'll take having a window to fill over having nothing of anything inside or out, wouldn't you say?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: You—!

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Now, now. You're not happy to calm down for a while, I see. How about this? If which foot forward first bothers you so much in this ball you know nothing about, I can be your lead for the dance.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: What complete shit are you on about?!

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: I'm thinking of bigger things. With this many nobles and merchants coming, if we can get their support, then forget just occupying one scant little Hillock, we could snatch the whole of Londinium—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Mandragora, time to hold still.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: At this point, can't you just let that grotty book of yours go? Do you even think for one second about anything important to The Leader or me?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: I'm not saying anything about your oh-so-helpless gait. I'm saying, take your rollercoaster babble and hold it still, and all that absurdity you're exhausting your little brain with too.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: You, telling me to hold it now? As if I could! Laying out and assigning roles, swallowing my sick to set this meeting up, how much of me do you think I've poured out for this plan?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: I couldn't wait since forever ago! I can't wait! For Dublinn's fires to burn this city through, rip this lie of a titan under our feet apart!

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: And you, huh? You and that shameless fake taking what should be the glory of The Leader—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: It is really, really, time for you to shut up now.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: At what point—was your job to make decisions for The Leader?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Tch—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Mm, it's me. Yes, we're still here.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Things have gotten a little interesting at long last.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Seems we've no need to scrap in here about whether your little schemes of insolence are feasible or not.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Is it news from that bastard?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Someone's sniffed out this location. I've a feeling it'll be more than your friendly little invitees coming to the meeting tonight.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: ...People from the army?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: More or less. My, my, maybe some of my acquaintances too.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Tch. God on high, I want to—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Put away your staff. You'll get your chance. But it won't be now.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: It's time we go, we've got other things to do. Leave it to her in here; we might be in for a good show before we know it.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Heheh... I was starting to fantasize about how it'd look if this horrible room broke down into slag.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Leader, I didn't imagine slippin' in would be as easy as this. Here I thought...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We'd have to find a way to infiltrate? Not out of the question. That said, go in the proper way, and it's more convenient to find a conversation partner.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Guess my friend at the barracks got some real precious information. Can't be that many who know about this meeting.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: A lot of secret aristocrat parties are held this way—they usually think of invitation letters as passé.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: So long as you have a channel to tap for info, plus a token as proof of identity, you have what you need to pass the doorstep.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: You never told me your family was all big famous nobility.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Does it make a difference?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: When I was in school, the noble students always stuck with their own. Course, they studied together, but after school, they never did much with the rest of us if they could help it.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Don't tell me you actually like all the pomp and formality? Ceremonial gowns you only wear once, the trending look changing every week, courtesy greetings ad nauseum.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Don't even remind me. Actually went to that kind of thing once or twice with a good friend, and just tryin' to remember which fork you use to eat first made my head want to explode on the spot.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Perfect, I'm not much of a fan either.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Even if I'm loath to admit it, just having this family name does come in handy once in a while.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Leader, the people comin' here today, are they all supporters of the spectre force?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ...I don't necessarily think so.

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: Mr. Williams, I finally get to meet you! I heard you were coming, and came bolting right over from County Peninsula, just to ask if you could sign the anthology in my collection here.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Of course, fine Lady, it would be my honor.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Seamus, my dearest great bard! Here you were.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: I just finished reading your newly published tales from history. Such fascinating writings. It was the first I learned that us Tarans had such a grand, storied past.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Thank you, but they're works of fantasy, adapted from an array of folk legends. The greatest value in my work is simply unearthing gems buried by sandstorms, all the better for more to see.

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: You truly are too modest. The Draco King Gaeil you penned, founding by himself the most radiant culture that was Tara—he stood grand and wise, so much so that my dreams are flush with emotion and he's part of them all—

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Yes, too true. In my eyes, you're alike to Leithanien's grand musicians, with the chance to make change to an entire era!

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Ha, ha... I must say you exaggerate.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: So long as you wanted, all of Victoria's publishers would be wide open to you, every one of them waiting to translate your works into the ink of different languages.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: And when that happens, every country across the land will realize our Taran culture has its own unique charm, not to be stifled by the ever-same grumble of Victoria's machines.

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: If only things could be so wonderful. If more and more international figures come to support us, our voices will be so much more easily heard by the dukedom and Parliament.

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: Right you are! I'm a Victorian citizen same as anyone else, but just because some great-great-great-grandfather of mine was King Gaeil's subject, suddenly I'm being asked to pay so much more inheritance tax! How preposterous!

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: Even so, Mr. Evans, you still give vigorous employ to plenty enough of our fellows, providing everyone the chance to gain their footing upon this city of grace.

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: No wonder you and your clan are the pride of us Tarans.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Ahah, quite right, our fellows. It's far from easy for them to find any respectable work. I hear they toil in the factories for a week, and only earn yea little coin.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Yet Victorian workers from other backgrounds are able to earn twice as much, in your factories.

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: Eh-hem...

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: Allow me to say something perhaps a little out of fashion—it's far from simple to have our neighbors of strength acknowledge us, isn't it?

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: Please, think about it, everyone. Were it only with its music and poems, how could Leithanien become the Leithanien of today?

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: Just as Leithanien has Casters that intimidate—

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: We Tarans must depend on more practical power if we want to gain recognition. Such as the... technological support of some friends from far away.

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: And by pure luck, I have just the tiniest means by which I receive sponsorship, and I would be overjoyed to take the opportunity to let the friends of the Baron share in it.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Hahah, you're absolutely spot-on! Any subsidy is of great importance. If you let it all pass you by, then no matter how deft your tongue, you watch for the day it dries up and lacks the power to express.

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: From that perspective, I'm the same as everyone here. We are all yearning for a whole new era—so, why not give a toast to this common dream of ours?

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: Truly, an evening to inspire... how strange, where did Mr. Williams get off to?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Good evening, Mr. Williams.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Greetings, ma'am.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I hope I'm not bothering you. Are you writing?

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Ha, ha... Just a small poem. It's been several days now, and I still haven't finished it.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: I was thinking this meeting would give me some inspiration, but it seems now there's still no forcing the muse.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: These settings always like to use up a person's energy too quickly. Do you also feel a little worn out?

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Ha-ha... caught red-handed. If it weren't for Charles—I mean, the Baron inviting me so ardently, I would've preferred to spend the night reading by my own fireplace.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Wouldn't we all? I bet every person willing to participate in this sort of thing is forced to for a living.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: I like that way of putting it. You're not a Taran, ma'am, are you?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You guess correctly. I imagine a Lupo's a rare sight among the residents here.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Ha-ha, I've inadvertently judged background by race.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Though you're deliberately choosing vocabulary we're more used to, your accent still exposes you—it's the accent only a Victorian noble receiving a standard Londinium education would have.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: No wonder you're a great bard. Extremely sharp.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: The first step to writing is observation. I can even tell, you and they have differing purposes for coming.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You're suspecting me?

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Suspecting what? I'm only here to exchange some ideas, and you're exchanging with me right now.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: No matter if I'm not a Taran?

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Precisely because you're not.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: A glass of malt liquor, thank you—would you like anything to drink, ma'am?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I'll be fine. Standing in the window breeze is plenty enough for me.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Then we'll continue our merry chat. What were we just saying?

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Right, yes. Words and writing were born for the purpose of exchange, including both conversations past and future, and this talk between you and I, here and now.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You're the one allowing for me. If you used Taran, I'd be as good as deaf.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Ha-ha—in this party, you'll be hard-pressed to hear any Taran.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It just clicked for me, actually. All the works of yours I've read are written in Victorian.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Rhyming confines a poet's imagination. Characteristically, Victoria's poems, when you read them, are very unlike Leithanien's.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: I much love reading poems written in Old Taran. Reading the writing is like touching upon, feeling another face of history.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: But I've no plans to pass myself off as anything.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: I grew up speaking Victorian, my thoughts are molded by the language, and if I started to write in Taran instead, I'd be a clown dancing in shoes far too big for him.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I hear there are many longing for the revival of Taran culture—

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Of course, I'm one of them.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Our city roams upon the land, this soil unchanging, yet at the same time, change constantly happening.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Perhaps a day will come when Taran once again becomes the building blocks of our children's minds, and I'd be willing to embrace such a transformation.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: And if—there were those who wished this change to be rapid, an explosion even reversive of the natural trend?

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: 'What is the use of an idea? You are planting a feather in the ground, imagining it growing into a fowlbeast.'

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: From the first poetry anthology you published. It's one of my particular favorites.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: That is my answer to this question of yours.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: In my own view, I can't, and have no thought to alter this soil. I'm simply the one trying hard to plant feathers.

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: And ideas fundamentally ought to be free, with no one who can interfere—each feather that grows in each person's heart may be totally unalike, just as we all have different hopes for the future of this great swathe of soil.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I understand, Mr. Williams.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Allow me to speak from the heart—it's been truly pleasant to chat with you.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Leader, somethin's not right.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Cello's lot have gone over forty minutes without sendin' anythin'.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Weren't they meant to be dealin' with the troops at the barracks? You told them they were to send a message every half hour. Right as we set off, Cello was even gripin' at me how this mission was too borin'.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: And on top of that... don't you feel it's a little too quiet all around?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I've been keepin' watch at the window. Ought to be able to see people goin' in and out of the plaza. But then all of a sudden, it was like somethin' happened, and everyone scarpered away.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Don't tell me... the ones tailing us before were the barracks'...
The ballroom doors are kicked open without warning.
Dozens of soldiers armed to the teeth come charging in.

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: Good heavens, what's happening? Why the sudden show of force?

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: You have the audacity to point weapons at me... do you understand who we are?

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: Who is it? Who let the secret out?!

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: Damn and blast... we need to get out of here, quick!

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: (Hurry, go inform Madam Mandragora, just say we've got trouble...)

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: (What?! You mean they're all gone? When did this happen? A whole hour ago?!)

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: (You useless...!)

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: All of you, stay where you are!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Ladies and gentlemen, yes, no mistake, you have been—utterly captured.
